card.job: Lay out a whole agent screen: past sessions, the thread and a docked composer.
card.purpose: The page layout for an AI agent. A session list sits in a side column, the thread scrolls in the middle at reading measure, and the composer docks at the bottom with the thread fading under it. With data-fill it takes the viewport height under the top bar. Below 760px the side column leaves and the thread takes the width.
useWhen: The product is a conversation with an agent and the screen is the agent: ask, watch it work, read the answer.
People return to earlier runs and need the session list beside the thread.

avoidWhen.when: The conversation is help or support inside another product screen.
One endpoint with options is tried through a request form and a response panel.
A page needs only a prompt box, not the whole screen.

states.name: no session column
states.how: omit .fd-agent-side; the grid collapses to one column

variants.useWhen: The agent is the whole page: height is the viewport minus the top bar, and the thread scrolls inside.

parts.role: The grid: optional side column plus the main column.
Holds the session list, with a hairline on its end edge.
The column with the top row, scroll area and dock.
A slim row for the title and page-level actions.
The scrolling thread, or the hero prompt when empty.
Pinned bottom area for the composer.
One muted line under the composer, such as "can be wrong".

card.job: Frame every signed-in screen with a sidebar, a top bar and a page.
card.purpose: The app shell: a sidebar on the left, a main column with the top bar and the page, and a mobile nav. The sidebar is expanded or a 64px icon rail; the choice is remembered. The shell is a size container, so under 900px of its own width the sidebar gives way to the top bar and a menu button. It also holds the floating support button.
useWhen: The product has several screens that share navigation, an account and a top bar.
A screen is a working page inside the product, not a single task on its own page.

avoidWhen.when: A single task on a page of its own: sign in, consent, a result.
A docs site with its own two-row top bar and contents column.
A marketing page with no signed-in navigation.

states.name: contained
states.how: data-contained; fills its parent box instead of the viewport

variants.useWhen: The default: icons with labels.
Dense work, such as a playground or a long log, where width matters more than labels.
The shell sits in a box, as in docs or a preview.
Render the saved sidebar state without animating on load.

parts.role: The root; a size container named fd-app.
The column to the right of the sidebar.
The drafted page column with 1px rails inside fd-page.
One registration mark where a hairline crosses a rail.

keyboard.does: Moves through the sidebar, top bar and page in markup order.

card.job: Ask whether the agent may run an action, with allow once, always allow and deny.
card.purpose: A one-line strip with an icon, the action in plain words (what, where, how much it costs) and up to three choices. It is the small form of the approval state of a tool call; use it when the permission is asked outside a tool call row.
useWhen: The agent wants to do something that costs credits or touches data and a person must say yes first.
A permission sits between turns, not inside a tool call row.

avoidWhen.when: The pending step is already a row in a run.
The action deletes or changes access and needs a typed or explicit confirmation.
The message is a notice with no choice to make.

parts.role: The strip; takes an icon first.
The question; bold the action and the cost.
The choices, usually Allow once, Always allow and Deny.

card.job: Return to the one obvious previous place.
card.purpose: A link with a left arrow and a label such as "Back to dashboard". The arrow travels a few pixels on hover. Use it when there is one place to return to, not a hierarchy.
useWhen: A detail or a result screen has one parent to return to.
A phone screen needs a way back to its list.

avoidWhen.when: The screen is several levels deep.
The action cancels or dismisses a task in a dialog.
The history is a flow.

keyboard.does: Follows the link.

card.job: Sign a surface with the product mark and name, an uploaded logo or a wordmark.
card.purpose: The brand is a mark and a name, set in a 40px row. A customer logo can replace the mark as an image of 24px, or a wide logo can replace both (up to 160px wide; it cannot shrink to the rail). A wordmark is an SVG in the current colour, for a caption or a line of text.
useWhen: The top of the sidebar or a centred screen needs the product identity.
A page says "Powered by" with a small wordmark.

avoidWhen.when: A person or a team needs an avatar.
A small rounded icon stands for an object, not the brand.
A label on a card or row.

variants.useWhen: A wordmark inside a caption or a line of small text.
The wordmark is the brand itself and takes the accent.

parts.role: The 36px mark, an inline SVG or a 24px image.
A wide logo that stands in for the mark and the name.
An SVG wordmark that takes the current colour.

keyboard.does: Follows the brand link.

card.job: Show where this screen sits and jump to a parent.
card.purpose: A list of links ending in the current page. Use it when a screen is several levels deep, such as a run inside a monitor. The last item is a span with aria-current="page". Wrap it in nav with aria-label="Breadcrumb".
useWhen: A screen is three or more levels deep and people need to go up to any parent.
The hierarchy is fixed: workspace, project, item.

avoidWhen.when: There is one obvious place to return to.
The path is a flow in a set order.
Content is paged.

parts.role: The nav; holds an ol of li items.

keyboard.does: Moves between the links.

card.job: Start an action or confirm a choice with one press.
card.purpose: The native button in Fire's soft style: a quiet fill that darkens on hover, with one primary per view. Variants and sizes are data attributes; loading, held and disabled come from aria-busy, aria-pressed, aria-expanded and disabled. On touch devices every size grows to a 40px target.
useWhen: An action runs on this page and nothing navigates: save, create, send, copy, retry.
A dialog, sheet or confirmation needs its confirm and cancel actions.
A toolbar needs icon-only actions (add data-icon-only and an aria-label).

avoidWhen.when: The action is a link to another page, or sits inside a sentence.
avoidWhen.instead: The text button (fd-btn-text), part of this component.

avoidWhen.when: Several related actions belong together as one control.
avoidWhen.instead: The button group (fd-btn-group), part of this component.

avoidWhen.when: One floating action stays visible while the page scrolls.
The user picks one option of several, or switches a setting on and off.
Delete or revoke runs without a confirmation step.
avoidWhen.instead: Put it behind a dialog or confirm; use the danger variant on the confirming button.

states.name: loading
states.how: aria-busy="true"; keeps the width and shows a spinner

states.name: held
states.how: aria-pressed="true" or aria-expanded="true"; uses the pressed fill

states.name: copied
states.how: data-state="done" on a fd-btn-swap child, set by fire.js for 1.4s after a copy

variants.useWhen: The one action the view exists for; at most one per view.
On a filled or busy surface where the default wash would disappear.
Dismissals and toolbar actions that should stay quiet.
A single upsell or confirm on a quiet panel; never beside a primary.
An accent-tinted action that is not the primary.
The confirming button of a destructive action, inside a confirmation.
A destructive action shown before any confirmation, such as Revoke in a row.
Inside dense rows and chips.
In toolbars and table rows.
Forms and dialogs that want a larger target.
A hero or a landing page call to action.
The button holds only an icon; it needs aria-label or data-fd-tooltip.
The button fills its row, as in a phone dialog footer.

parts.role: The button; a button, a or input element.
Wraps two children that swap in place, as a copy button's label and its Copied confirmation.
Joins related buttons into one control.
An action written as text inside a sentence or a card footer.

keyboard.does: Activates the button.

card.job: Talk with an AI assistant and a support person in one thread, with rich replies.
card.purpose: A support and help chat. A head says who is answering, an optional banner flags incidents, a body shows one view (home, conversation, history or offline), and the composer is pinned to the bottom. The AI replies in prose, a person in a bubble beside their face, and messages carry blocks such as forms, cards and approvals. It docks, floats, fills a page or pushes it. Under 640px it is a full-screen sheet.
useWhen: Customers ask for help from inside the product or on docs and marketing pages.
An AI answers first and a person can take over in the same thread.
A help page needs a persistent conversation with history and an offline form.

avoidWhen.when: An agent that does the person's work, with tool calls, plans and results.
Only a prompt box on a page.
A short question in a floating card with no history.
Comments or notes on a record.

states.name: expanded
states.how: data-expanded; a 760px panel or a taller popup

states.name: closed conversation
states.how: data-disabled; the composer is disabled with a reason

states.name: dragging
states.how: data-dragging; the file drop overlay shows

states.name: remembered
states.how: open state and mode saved per browser session; data-persist="false" opts out

variants.useWhen: Help from anywhere in the console: 420px, docked right, over the page.
Marketing and docs pages: a 400px card that grows out of the launcher.
An embedded help page or a full-page inbox: fills its box and is always open.
Long sessions where the person works and asks together: a 400px column that pushes the page.
The AI is answering; the disclaimer shows.
A person from support is answering.
Nobody is in; the head says when they are back.
Waiting for a person; the head shows the place in line.
A new conversation: greeting and up to four starter questions.
The thread.
Past conversations with their state.
The form that takes a message when nobody is in.
A wider panel or taller popup for long answers.
Position inside the nearest positioned box, for docs and previews.

parts.role: The root; an empty one is filled with the default support chat by chat.js.
The 52px head: who answers, the status line and the icon actions.
An incident strip under the head; tone is warning, danger or info.
The composer, reply strip, closed line and disclaimer.
The "New messages" pill when scrolled up.
The overlay shown while a file is dragged over.
The one-time offer of help near the launcher.

keyboard.does: Sends the message.
Adds a new line.
In an empty composer, edits your last message.
Cancels an edit or quote, or closes a floating chat.

card.job: Open and close the chat from a floating button with an unread count.
card.purpose: The floating action button for the chat. Its chat icon turns and fades into a chevron while the chat is open; an unread count pops in beside it. Add data-fd-chat-toggle with the chat id and it keeps aria-expanded and aria-controls in sync, and focus returns to it when the chat closes. A teaser can offer help once after a delay.
useWhen: The chat floats over the page and needs a button that is always in reach.
Unread replies should show on a button when the chat is closed.

avoidWhen.when: A floating action that is not the chat.
A chat that sits in a column or fills a page and is always open.
A button in a toolbar that opens a menu.

states.name: unread
states.how: the badge shows the count; setUnread(n) updates it and the accessible name

variants.useWhen: Pin to the bottom-right corner of the viewport.
Pin inside the nearest positioned box instead of the viewport.
The icon shown while the chat is closed.
The icon shown while the chat is open.

parts.role: One of two stacked icons, data-role open or close.
A pill used for a starter question or a quick reply.

keyboard.does: Opens or closes the chat.

card.job: View a chat image full size and step through the others.
card.purpose: A large dialog that opens when a person clicks an image in a chat message. It shows the image, a counter such as 2 of 4, and Previous and Next buttons. chat.js creates one shared dialog for the page. It is a dialog with a media area, so it traps focus and closes on Escape.
useWhen: A chat message holds images and people should see them larger.

avoidWhen.when: Images in a gallery outside a chat.
A zoomable figure in documentation.
A file that is not an image.

parts.role: The dialog; it is also an fd-dialog.

keyboard.does: Shows the next image.
Shows the previous image.
Closes the lightbox.

card.job: Show who said what in a chat, and carry blocks such as forms, cards and approvals.
card.purpose: One message in a chat. The person speaks from a grey bubble on the right, the AI in prose beside a spark, a person from support in a white bubble beside their face, and the system in small muted lines. Messages from one author within two minutes join into a run. The body is a stack of blocks, each built from another Fire component. Only the latest message of the person shows its delivery state.
useWhen: A support or help chat shows turns from the person, the AI, an agent and the system.
An answer should hold a form, a card, a list of choices or an approval, not only text.

avoidWhen.when: A turn in an agent thread.
A notification outside a conversation.
A single tool step.

states.name: typing
states.how: data-typing; the indicator at the end of the thread

variants.useWhen: The person's own message: grey bubble on the right.
The AI: unboxed prose beside a spark.
A support person: white bubble beside their face with name and role.
A date, join, handover or resolution line.
Same author within two minutes; chat.js sets it.
Prose, lists, code and citations.
Offer up to three likely answers that send themselves.
One to three buttons for what to do next.
An object worth opening: a docs article or a plan.
The answer depends on which one; radio rows with meta.
Collect a few details without leaving the thread.
An action that moves money, deletes or changes access asks first.
Hand over to a person with the wait and place in line.
Ask once, at the end, how the conversation went.

parts.role: The column with head, body and meta.
One block in the body; data-type picks the kind. Other kinds: carousel, details, table, code, attachment, sources, tool, steps, metric, schedule, notice.
Copy, react, reply and good or bad answer on hover or focus.
The delivery line under the latest message.

keyboard.does: Reveals the message actions and moves through the blocks.
Activates a focused action, option or button in a block.

card.job: Tick one or more options, or a yes that saves with the form.
card.purpose: 16px box with a 4px radius and one hairline. Checked fills with the accent and draws a tick; indeterminate draws a dash. The label is part of the control, so the whole line is the target. data-fd-checkall on a parent shows indeterminate and ticks or clears its children.
useWhen: Several options may be chosen from a fixed set.
A yes or no is saved with the rest of the form, not at once.
A select-all parent controls a group of children.

avoidWhen.when: A setting takes effect the moment it changes.
Exactly one of a few options is chosen.
Each option needs a title, a sentence or a price.
A table row is selected; use the table's own selection.

states.name: indeterminate
states.how: input.indeterminate = true, or data-fd-checkall on a parent

parts.role: The label that wraps the input.
The drawn box; forms.js adds the tick and dash.
The tick path inside the box.

keyboard.does: Toggles the focused checkbox.

card.job: Browse a catalogue by category.
card.purpose: A category strip, lighter than tabs: no underline, just ink. The selected chip turns weight 450 and its width is reserved up front so neighbours never shift. Link chips mark the current category with aria-current="page"; button chips are single-select with aria-pressed and fire fd:change. It scrolls sideways and fades at the clipped edge.
useWhen: A catalogue, gallery or template list is narrowed by category.
There are more categories than a segmented control holds.

avoidWhen.when: The items switch views of one object.
There are two to five exclusive options.
The filters combine and apply together.
The items are settings pages.

states.name: current
states.how: aria-current="page" on a link chip, or aria-pressed="true" on a button chip

variants.useWhen: Content is clipped at the start.
Content is clipped at the end.
Content is clipped at both ends.

parts.role: One category; a link or a button.

keyboard.does: Moves between chips.
Select a button chip; Enter follows a link chip.

card.job: Choose from options that each need a title and a sentence.
card.purpose: A selectable card over a real radio or checkbox. Selected is one accent hairline, a faint accent wash and a check. Put the whole decision in the card: a title, one sentence and at most one figure on the right. Lay out as a list for a few options or as a grid (data-layout="grid") for scannable sets.
useWhen: Plans, permission levels or modes where each option needs explaining.
Each option has a price or one key figure.
Several of a fixed set may be picked, with enough to say about each (checkbox inside).

avoidWhen.when: The options are plain labels.
The options are plain labels and several may be ticked.
The choice filters what is shown and has no explanation.
The card opens something instead of selecting.

variants.useWhen: Many cards that people scan side by side.

parts.role: Groups cards; carries role="radiogroup" for single choice.
The label that wraps the input.
A figure on the right, such as a price.

keyboard.does: Native: move between the radio cards of a group.
Selects or toggles the focused card.

card.job: Edit raw code or JSON that has to be valid.
card.purpose: A text area in the code face with a head showing the language and an optional Format button. Tab inserts two spaces. data-fd-json checks the value on blur and on submit and writes the parser's reason and line into the field's error. Without script it is a plain text area. It is for the few places raw code is the input, never a stand-in for a control that fits better.
useWhen: An expert overrides configuration by hand and the value is JSON.
The input is code and needs checking: a template, a schema, a config override.

avoidWhen.when: The value is a list, a map or a choice that a control fits.
The value is a map of names to values.
The text is prose.
The code is shown, not edited.

states.name: invalid JSON
states.how: aria-invalid="true" with the reason in .fd-field-error, set by data-fd-json

states.name: ready
states.how: data-ready set by the script; the Format button shows

parts.role: Row with the language and the Format button.

keyboard.does: Inserts two spaces.
Leaves the field.

card.job: Keep a narrow block readable on a wide page.
card.purpose: A bounded column with a maximum width (data-size xs, sm, md, lg or xl) that stays centred when data-align="center". Use it so text and forms stop at a readable measure while the page stays wide.
useWhen: A form, an article or an empty state sits on a wide page and should not stretch.
A page has one main column in the middle.

avoidWhen.when: A form should set its own width.
A main area has a side panel.
Content is in equal columns.

variants.useWhen: A very narrow block.
A narrow block, such as a sign-in card.
A reading width.
A wide reading column.
The widest column.
The column sits in the middle of the page.

card.job: Pick from a long list by typing to filter it.
card.purpose: A text field with a listbox that uses the Popover API, so it layers above everything and closes on outside clicks. Type to filter, arrow keys to move, Enter to choose. Options are role="option" rows with an optional icon, description and mono meta. The multiple variant keeps choices as removable tokens. Fires fd:open, fd:close, fd:select and fd:change.
useWhen: The list is long enough that people need to type to find an item.
Each option needs an icon, a description or a meta label (a model, a team member).
Several items may be chosen and shown as tokens (data-multiple).

avoidWhen.when: The list is short and plain.
People may enter values that are not on a list.
The choice runs a command or jumps to a page.
The options are two to four visible labels.

states.name: open
states.how: data-state="open" on the wrapper; the listbox is shown

states.name: multiple
states.how: data-multiple on the wrapper; choices become tokens

states.name: no match
states.how: data-empty="No matches" text shows when the filter finds nothing

parts.role: The wrapper; carries data-fd-combobox and data-name.

keyboard.does: Opens the list, then moves to the next option.
Opens the list at the last option, then moves up.
Chooses the active option, or closes the list.
Closes the list.
Closes the list and moves on.
In multiple mode with an empty field: removes the last token.

card.job: Ask the agent for something and attach context, sources and a model.
card.purpose: The prompt form for an agent. A textarea grows to 240px, then scrolls. A row of tools holds the model chip, attachments, source toggles and the send button. The send button is a grey dot with no text, the accent with text, and a stop square while the agent runs. Sending fires fd:submit.
useWhen: The person writes a prompt for an agent and may choose a model, sources or files.
A hero prompt needs example suggestions that fill the field.
A playground endpoint needs one card of rows (input, sources, actions).

avoidWhen.when: A short free-text answer inside a form.
A conversation with a person or support, with a reply strip and file drop.
A single-line query that filters a list or jumps to a page.

states.name: ready
states.how: data-ready, set by agent.js while the field has text

states.name: running
states.how: data-state="running"; send becomes a stop square

states.name: focused
states.how: data-focus; the accent halo, shown statically

states.name: disabled
states.how: disabled on the input and buttons

variants.useWhen: One card of rows for a single endpoint: input, source chips and a footer with the actions.
The composer sits inside a surface that already has an edge, so it draws none.
A quiet composer in a dense panel, without the raised card.
A compact composer inside a chat or a narrow panel.
The model menu opens upward because the composer sits at the bottom of the screen.

parts.role: A toggle or action button; aria-pressed marks a source that is on.
The round send button; the stop square while running.
Chips for files above the input, each with progress and a remove button.
The empty-state wrapper that holds a heading, the composer and suggestions.
The button that opens the model menu (a native popover).
The menu of models, one radio item each.
A ring and percentage for how full the context is.
A mono line of credits, tokens and pages used.
A "Stop generating" button outside the composer.

keyboard.does: Sends; cancel fd:submit to keep the text.
Adds a new line.
Sends.
In a playground form, runs the request.

card.job: Show a value people copy, such as an address or an ID.
card.purpose: A read-only value with a copy button, in the same field shape. Copy always copies the whole data-value, and a check shows for a moment (fd:copy). data-mask="end" keeps the readable start and the last few characters with dots between; it stays masked with no reveal button, so leave the button out when nobody may see the value.
useWhen: A webhook URL, endpoint, ID or an invite link is shown for copying.
An address is recognised by its last characters (data-mask="end").

avoidWhen.when: The value is secret and may be revealed or rotated.
The value is a command or code with several lines.
The value is editable.
The copy button sits inside a field people also type in.

states.name: copied
states.how: data-state="copied" for a moment after the copy

variants.useWhen: Show the start up to data-mask-from, eight dots and the last few characters.
Keep the first and last eight characters.
Show only dots.

parts.role: The wrapper; carries data-fd-secret and data-value.
An optional label inside the field.
The part that shortens with an ellipsis.
The part that is never cut off.

keyboard.does: On the copy button: copies the value.

card.job: Stop the page until the person finishes or dismisses one task.
card.purpose: A native dialog opened with showModal(): the page behind is washed out and blurred, focus moves into it and returns to the trigger. Escape, a close button and a backdrop click close it, and fd:close fires once per close whichever way it ended. Below 640px it becomes a bottom sheet you can drag down. Multi-step flows use sections with data-step.
useWhen: The task must finish or be dismissed before the page makes sense again: create a key, choose providers.
A short form needs its own focus, with confirm and cancel at the foot.
A flow has two or three steps, such as create then show the secret once.

avoidWhen.when: A destructive action needs the person to type a name before it runs.
The content is a side panel the person may leave open while working.
The content is a short list of actions on one trigger.
The content is a summary or a small picker that closes on outside click.
The message is feedback after an action and needs no decision.

states.name: open
states.how: openDialog(id), a trigger with data-fd-dialog-open="id", or showModal()

states.name: persistent
states.how: data-static on the dialog keeps backdrop clicks from closing it

states.name: reset on open
states.how: data-reset on the dialog resets its forms each time it opens

variants.useWhen: A confirmation or a one-field form (400px).
A form with several fields or a short list (640px).
A picker with a toolbar and a grid (800px).

parts.role: The heading; focus lands here when the body has no field.
The scrolling content; edge shadows show when it overflows.
The actions: cancel first, the confirming button last.
The corner close button; carries data-fd-dialog-close.
Step dots in a multi-step dialog.

keyboard.does: Closes the dialog.
Moves between controls inside the dialog; focus does not leave it.

card.job: Separate two groups with a hairline.
card.purpose: A one-pixel rule in the faint line colour. data-vertical makes it a vertical rule that stretches to the height of a row. With fd-grow it fills a row on either side of a word such as "or".
useWhen: Two groups in a toolbar or a menu need a quiet break.
A row reads "or" between two rules.

avoidWhen.when: Rows in a list need lines between them.
A card needs a boundary.
Form fields group under a title.

variants.useWhen: A rule between items of a row, as in a top bar.

card.job: Build a documentation site in the product's own look: nav, article, contents and footer.
card.purpose: The docs shell: a two-row top bar (tools and section tabs), a neutral nav, a reading column of 720px or less with an On this page rail, and an article footer with Was this helpful, the pager and the site footer. Declare the page with data-docs-shell on body; the page supplies only its article. It also holds search, the changelog and the home page.
useWhen: The product has guides, SDK pages and an API reference that should read like the product.
A page needs the docs header, nav and contents column around an article.

avoidWhen.when: The signed-in app shell with a sidebar and top bar.
A single help article inside a chat.
One long page of text without navigation.

states.name: contained
states.how: data-contained; the shell scrolls inside a box of height --h

states.name: no contents column
states.how: data-toc="false" on the body, for reference pages

states.name: no footer
states.how: data-foot="false" on the body, for landing pages

variants.useWhen: The shell is a box that scrolls inside itself, as in previews.
An article that needs more than the 720px reading column, such as a reference table.
The top bar's first row: brand, search, repository, theme, sign up.
The top bar's second row: section tabs in ink.
The breadcrumb bar that opens the nav sheet under 900px.
A GET tag in the nav or an endpoint bar.
A POST tag.
A PUT tag.
A PATCH tag.
A DELETE tag, labelled DEL to keep the column narrow.

parts.role: The shell; a size container named fd-doc.
The search pill that opens the command palette.
The neutral nav; the current page is an 8% ink pill.
Eyebrow, 36px title, lead and the Copy page split button.
Was this helpful, with a form that opens on No.
The docs home: big search and ways in.
A guide card with a time to read.

keyboard.does: Opens the docs search palette.
Opens a nav group or follows a link.
Moves through the top bar, nav and article.

card.job: Point readers to the assistant at the end of a docs section.
card.purpose: A one-line callout with a sparkle, a bold lead ("Tip: ask the assistant.") and a button that opens the command palette or the chat. It stays at the same width as the reading column and sits last in a section. Use at most one per screen.
useWhen: A docs section ends and an assistant has read the pages and can answer in the reader's language.
A reference page should offer one way to ask a question.

avoidWhen.when: A note, tip or warning about the content itself.
A system-wide message above a page.
A full conversation.

parts.role: The row; icon first, button last.
The message with a bold lead.

keyboard.does: Activates the button.

card.job: Fan out from an overview to the pages beneath it with link cards.
card.purpose: A grid of fd-card[data-interactive] items, each with an icon, a title and one line. They are flush with the page until hovered. The grid has one to six columns and collapses on narrow widths. The icon is a plain glyph, never a logo.
useWhen: A docs overview or an intro page leads to three to six places to read next.
A section index lists its pages with a line each.

avoidWhen.when: A catalog of items with media, price or state.

card.job: Keep one primary action in reach while the page scrolls.

card.job: Give a control a label, a hint and room for one error.

An API parameter form is generated from a schema (data-variant="schema").

A switch or checkbox carries its own label text.

card.job: Add files by dropping them or browsing.
card.purpose: A dashed, sunken area that is also a button: click or press Enter to browse, or drop files. Dragging over it turns the line accent. states.name: error

Progress, ready or the reason it failed.

card.job: Lay out fields and actions in a form that stays readable.
card.purpose: The form container: it stops at a readable width on its own (data-size sm, lg or full) and holds rows, columns and an actions bar. fd-form-row puts a label and what it does on the left and the control on the right; fd-form-cols fills the body in columns. Changes should trigger an unsaved-changes bar (data-fd-dirty, data-variant="sticky").

card.job: Group the fields of a long form under a title.
card.purpose: One titled group in a long create or edit form: a narrow head with a title and one line on the left (it stays in view while the body scrolls) and the fields on a white surface beside it. Below about 720px of form width the head stacks above the body. Use it inside a form with data-size="full".

A narrower body.
A wider body.

parts.role: The white surface holding the fields.

card.job: Lay out equal columns that fill the width and reflow.
card.purpose: An auto-filling grid. data-min sets the narrowest column (a size token from 4xs to 6xl, or full), data-cols the most columns, and data-span on a child covers several columns (or full). It drops columns on narrow screens by itself, so markup never sets a width.

One child needs to span several columns (data-span).

A rule must fill the space on either side of an "or".

parts.role: The class on the child that grows.

card.job: Draw a small symbol beside a label or on a button.
card.purpose: A 16px line icon from Fire's sprite, written as <i data-icon="name"> and drawn once at start (or as the fd-icon element with icon="name"). Sizes are 12, 14, 16, 20, 24 or 32 (plus sm and lg); tone sets its colour. It is decorative: name the control that holds it with a label. Change it with setIcon(el, name).

An empty state or a tile needs one glyph.

card.job: Type one line of text, a URL, a key or a number.
card.purpose: The native input in Fire's field skin: a white surface, a 1px line drawn inside the box so nothing shifts between states, 36px tall. Hover darkens the line, focus swaps it for the accent and adds a halo, aria-invalid turns it danger. It also works as a span in the same shape to show a value people read but do not edit.

card.job: Put an icon, prefix, unit or button inside one field.
card.purpose: One field with affixes: the group carries the single hairline and focus halo, and a bare fd-input lives inside it. Affixes are an icon, a text prefix, a unit, a chevron or a small ghost button one step below the field size. The same group holds the input of a combobox.

card.job: Show a list of options a person can choose from.
card.purpose: The option list a combobox opens, and the list inside any picker: fd-option rows with a check for the selected one, an optional description and mono meta, group labels and an empty message. card.job: Show that something small is loading with a ring, dots, bars or a text frame.
card.purpose: Loaders for work too small or too unpredictable to sketch. A ring goes inside controls and small panels. A braille frame or dots go beside a sentence that says what is happening. Equaliser bars show a stream receiving data. fd-pending shows an optimistic change at half strength until the server confirms it. Under reduced motion they hold still.

A stream is receiving data and needs a quiet live mark.
A change shows at once at half strength and settles when the server confirms.
